title: Adaptive burst-decay and KV cache throttling to contain noisy tenants in Dedicated clusters
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Following the March 8 Dedicated cluster capacity incident where a single tenant's workload increased short-lived peak token generation and caused KV cache thrashing and reservation exhaustion, we need a targeted mitigation that combines per-tenant burst decay (a token-bucket that decays faster after sustained bursts) with KV cache throttling for noisy tenants. Goal: prevent single-tenant spikes from evicting other tenants' reservations or causing tail-latency spikes, while preserving short, legitimate bursts for interactive customers. This ticket scopes prototyping, telemetry validation, canary rollout, and runbook updates.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: A customer workload with high parallelism amplified repeated long-context generation which depleted shared KV cache and consumed burst credits faster than reservations accounted for. The eviction cascade exposed a gap between burst accounting and cache pressure signals. Impact: multiple tenants experienced elevated 95th/99th latency and a handful of reservation evictions; automated autoscaling could not react quickly due to conservative cooldown settings. Existing burst policy allowed immediate replenishment that enabled oscillation when two noisy tenants alternated bursts. Outcome: implemented short-term static throttles; long-term solution required.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant burst token-bucket with configurable decay period implemented in the allocator/runtime and covered by unit tests
KV cache pressure metric (per-tenant approximate footprint) surfaced in console and used to gate burst replenishment
End-to-end telemetry: SLO dashboards show a reduction in 95th/99th tail latency during synthetic noisy tenant tests (>=40% improvement vs baseline)
Canary rollout plan and automated rollback if error rate or latency increases by >15% for canary tenants
Runbook updated with detection query, mitigation commands, and postmortem link
implementation_steps: Design: finalize token-bucket decay formula and config knobs (initial proposal: half-life decay with exponential backoff on repeated bursts)
Runtime: add per-tenant burst-account state and decay background worker; wire to admission controller
KV: instrument approximate per-tenant KV usage (LRU footprints + request counters) and export to telemetry
Policy: gate automatic burst replenishment when tenant KV footprint > threshold OR eviction-rate > X/min
Testing: unit tests for decay logic, integration tests with synthetic multi-tenant loadbench
Canary: deploy to 1 Dedicated cluster pool with 5 opt-in tenants and scheduled synthetic noisy jobs
Observability: build dashboard panels and alert rule (burst-replenish-failure, high-eviction-rate), add to console route for tenant ops
Rollout: gradual ramp to 25% clusters then 100%, with 30-minute cooldown between steps
Docs: update runbook, API docs for burst knobs, and internal design doc link
telemetry_queries: kv_footprint_bytes{tenant=~".*"} // approximate per-tenant KV memory in bytes

rollback_plan: If canary shows increased errors or 95th latency regresses by >15% for canary tenants: 1) disable burst-decay feature flag for the cluster via runtime config 2) revert KV throttling gates 3) restore previous autoscaling thresholds 4) escalate and collect debug traces. Target rollback time < 10 minutes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive decay could hurt genuine interactive bursts -> Mitigation: conservative default decay half-life (30s) and test coverage with interactive scenarios
Risk: Telemetry undercounting KV occupancy leads to false positives -> Mitigation: use conservative thresholds and fall back to request-rate gating
Risk: Complexity increases operational burden -> Mitigation: expose feature-flag and admin knobs plus automated alerts and runbook steps
